explainer.recovery: Next you get a recovery code. Write it on paper. It is the only other way in if you lose every passkey or forget the passphrase.

privacy.title: Privacy and security
privacy.intro: Petty encrypts your drawers on your device. The server stores ciphertext it cannot open. Here is exactly what it can and cannot see.
sees: Your email and display name, and those of people you share with.
How many drawers you have and how many lines each holds.
Who shares which drawer with whom, and with which role.
When each entry was written, by whom, on which line, and whether it was a count or a reversal — never the amount, the comment or the line's name.
The size of each encrypted record, rounded up to 256-byte steps.

Backups are your operator's choice: this app ships none. If your operator backs up the database, a copy holds the same ciphertext, your email and your encrypted vault — ask them how long copies are kept, including after an account is deleted.
If you let your browser's password manager save the vault passphrase, that manager (and its cloud sync) holds it too. That is your choice, not the server's.
defends: Anyone reading the database or a backup: drawer content, photos and vaults are ciphertext only. They still see the account and activity details listed above.
Anyone changing the database: moved, swapped or deleted entries are detected.
A compromised server: it holds no keys and cannot read drawer content.
A lost phone: the vault stays locked without the passphrase and locks itself after 24 hours.
A removed member: after removal the drawer key is replaced; they cannot read anything written afterwards.
not: Whoever serves this website could serve a version that steals your passphrase. Strict browser rules narrow this, they do not remove it.

When sign-in runs through Clerk, Clerk decides who may sign in. Whoever controls Clerk could sign in as you, but still needs your passphrase or passkey to open your drawers. Its code is built into this app at a fixed version and never loaded from elsewhere.

An access token you make for a tool (Settings → Access tokens) reads every drawer you can open, including drawers shared with you later, and a writing token can add entries and edit tags and places. Whoever holds the token string has that access until it expires or you revoke it. Treat it like a key.
Anyone you share a drawer with can read and copy everything in it. Removing them stops future access only.
A member with write access can also damage a drawer's history (the app then shows those records as tampered, but their content is gone). Share with people you trust.
A security bug in this app itself.
A forgotten passphrase with no recovery code: nobody can help, by design.

private.title: Private by design
private.body: Your drawers are encrypted on your device. The server only ever sees ciphertext.

shared.title: Share with people you trust
shared.body: Everyone who touches the cash sees the same drawer. Writers add entries; readers only look.

places.title: Places, not piles
places.body: Kitchen › shelf › tin. Put every drawer in its place; move a room and its drawers follow.

currencies.title: Currencies and things
currencies.body: Zloty and euro side by side — plus countable things like keys or documents. Tag any line and filter by tag.

verify.title: Count, confirm, never erase
verify.body: After a real count, confirm the drawer state. Mistakes are reversed, never deleted; the history stays honest.

passkey.title: Passkey first, works offline
passkey.body: Face ID, Touch ID or Windows Hello opens your vault. Installs like an app and keeps working without a network.

crypto.device: Everything is encrypted on your device (AES-256) before it is sent. Names, amounts, comments, photos — all of it.
crypto.server: The server stores locked boxes it cannot open. We could not show you your data if we wanted to.
crypto.safety: Every member has a safety number. Compare it once in person and no one can silently stand in the middle.
crypto.recovery: A passkey or a passphrase opens your data; a one-time recovery code is the spare key. We can reset neither.
crypto.chain: Entries form a tamper-evident chain: removing or changing history is detectable.

steps.one: Make a drawer for each place you keep cash, put it in its room or shelf, and put in what is there now.
steps.two: Add or withdraw with two taps whenever money moves. Reverse mistakes.
steps.three: Count the drawer now and then and confirm it. Share it with the people who use it.

see.a: No. Amounts and names are encrypted on your device. The server stores unreadable boxes, and that is verifiable in the browser.

places.q: Can I group drawers by room?
places.a: Yes. Places are a tree — house › kitchen › shelf — and every drawer sits in one of them. The home screen groups by room, and you can drag a place to another room; its drawers follow.

lost.q: What if I lose my passkey or forget the passphrase?
lost.a: Another passkey, the passphrase or the recovery code opens the vault. If all are lost, nobody — including us — can decrypt your data; a drawer member can re-share a shared drawer with you.

undo.q: Can I undo a change to a drawer?
undo.a: Yes. Entries are never erased: a mistake is reversed by a new entry. Changes to names, items, tags and places are kept for 30 days, and the drawer's owner can put an earlier version back.

cost.a: Petty is free software (AGPL-3.0) — you can run your own for nothing. If whoever runs a hosted instance ever charges for it, they must tell you clearly first.

phone.a: Petty installs from the browser (Add to Home Screen) and works offline like a native app, on iPhone and Android.

ai.title: Use Petty with AI
ai.intro: Ask an AI app about your drawers, or have it add an entry for you. A small program on your own computer holds an access token, opens your keys there and gives the app a few tools. The Petty server still sees only ciphertext.
tokenSteps: Open Settings → Access tokens → New token.
Give it a name, and choose whether it may add entries.
Confirm with your passkey or vault passphrase.
Copy the token. It is shown once only.
desktopSteps: Download the add-on below and open it. Claude Desktop installs it.
When it asks, paste this Petty address and your token.
On a Mac, allow network access if asked, then restart Claude Desktop.

Paste the printed block into the app's MCP settings, and put your token in place of petty_pat_….

honest: The token and your keys stay on your computer. The server never sees the secret half of the token.
Whatever you ask reaches the AI model, because you asked it.
Text in your drawers is shown to the model as quoted data, and a change is always a separate tool the app can ask you to approve.
To stop it, revoke the token in Settings → Access tokens.
A phone app cannot run this program yet.
